title: Redwood data retention demo - Haven Financial
summary: Redwood walkthrough of data handling and retention controls: request storage toggles, logging redaction, PII detection, KMS integration, audit logs, and deletion/export flows. Customer is evaluating hosted vs dedicated/private deployment for payments data and needs SOC2, SSO, and data residency assurances. Next steps: send SOC2/report, retention quickstart, and schedule POC kickoff and benchmark.

transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-11-25
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~56 minutes
Attendees: Ava (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Jules (Redwood SE), Lena (Haven Head of Platform), Miguel (Haven Security), Priya (CTO), Ethan (SRE)

Summary (auto): Redwood demo focusing on data retention and handling controls; included console walkthrough and API examples for request storage toggles, logging redaction, and KMS integration.

[00:00] Ava: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intros, and we'll jump into the data-handling and retention controls demo. Samir and Jules will run the console and API examples.
[00:22] Lena: Thanks, Ava. Quick context - Haven is looking at putting inference on payments metadata. Primary concern is ceding PII and not keeping transaction-level text. We're evaluating hosted vs dedicated.
[00:40] Miguel: Yeah security's main ask is ability to turn off request storage, strong redaction, and KMS support. Also audit logs for compliance and the ability to purge records on demand.
[00:55] Samir: Totally, we'll cover request storage toggles, logging redaction rules, PII detection, and KMS key management. Also show how the console surfaces retention windows and legal-hold capabilities.
[01:15] Jules: I'll share my screen - console > project > data controls. Note sometimes the auto-captions call our Optimize product 'Redwood Opti-mize' or 'room wood optimizer' - ignore that, it's just the captioner.
[01:35] [screen share noise]
[01:40] Jules: At the top you can see 'Request Storage' with three states - store for analytics, store for debugging (redacted), and never store. We'll toggle from default (store redacted) to never store for this demo so no request payloads are persisted.
[01:58] Priya: When you say 'never store' does that also remove tokens from logs and analytics?
[02:05] Jules: Good question. 'Never store' prevents request/response payloads from being persisted to our long-term object store; we still emit minimal telemetry (latency, token counts) for SLOs but that is aggregated and not tied to raw text. If you need no telemetry, there's an option for reduced metrics.
[02:22] Ethan: Is that aggregated telemetry encrypted, and can we route it through our VPC / private monitoring?
[02:30] Samir: Metrics are encrypted in transit and at rest by default. For Dedicated and Private deployments we can route metrics into your VPC or forward to your monitoring. Also we support customer-managed KMS for key control.
[02:45] [crosstalk] Miguel: So KMS - do you support HSM-backed keys?
[02:52] Samir: Yes, we integrate with cloud KMS providers and HSMs for Dedicated/Private. The hosted offering supports customer-managed keys via AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault.
[03:05] Lena: Walk us through redaction - automatic PII detection and manual rules?
[03:12] Jules: We provide a PII detection pipeline that flags common identifiers (SSN, PAN, email, phone). You can apply policy actions: mask, remove, or route for manual review. There are prebuilt regex rules and you can upload custom patterns. I'll show the API sample.
[03:34] [Jules pastes API snippet]
[03:38] Jules: Example call: POST /v1/generate with header Redwood-Data-Retention: never-store, and a body-level flag redaction: {policy: "mask_sensitive"}. The console quickstart includes curl and SDK examples. Caveat: transcription may show 'Redewood' or similar in the captions.
[03:58] Miguel: For masking, does that happen before anything hits disk or logs? We're worried about transient writes.
[04:05] Samir: Masking is applied server-side in-memory before any persistence step. If you set never-store, nothing is written to object storage. Our ephemeral logs still have truncated IDs for correlation and are retained only per your retention window, configurable.
[04:21] Priya: How do you handle request replay for debugging if we turn off storage?
[04:27] Jules: We offer a debug-mode that can be enabled for selected requests or sessions which stores a redacted snapshot for a short TTL (configurable per project). There's also an audit-log export that includes metadata (not raw text) for incident review.
[04:45] Lena: Ok. What about legal hold? If we're required to retain records for an investigation, can we override deletions?
[04:52] Samir: Yes, legal-hold is available as a separate policy. You can lock specific request IDs or sessions and they won't be purged until the hold is released. We log all hold actions in the audit trail.
[05:08] Miguel: Auditing - is there a tamper-evident audit log?
[05:12] Samir: Audit logs are append-only and signed. For Dedicated/Private we can integrate with your SIEM and forward logs in near-real time. The hosted choice stores audit logs in encrypted buckets and provides export via S3/Blob.
[05:28] [pause; background noise]
[05:40] Ava: Quick demo of the API toggle - I'll run a sample where we send a payment description and set retention header to never-store. Jules, Samir, you can narrate.
[05:50] Ava (typing): curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <key>' -H 'Redwood-Request-Storage: never' -d '{"prompt":"Refund request for card 4111 1111 1111 1111..."}'
[06:15] Samir: The response comes back and we show no raw text persisted. The request id is returned for correlation so you can reference it in support cases but the payload is not present in storage.
[06:30] Miguel: Suppose we need selective retention like keep summaries only, or keep embeddings but not text - is that possible?
[06:38] Jules: Yup. You can configure per-route policies: retain embeddings for analytics, strip text, or store only anonymized summaries. The Optimize toolkit can auto-suggest policies based on your workload to reduce cost while preserving signal.
[06:55] Lena: Can policy be applied by route or token-level? We have different flows for dispute resolution vs regular receipts.
[07:03] Samir: Policies are applied at the project/route level and can be overridden per-request with headers or SDK flags. For fine-grained control you can set roles and let certain services opt into 'retain for N days' while others are never stored.
[07:18] Priya: How about data residency - we operate in EU - can you guarantee storage in region?
[07:24] Samir: Yes. For Hosted we offer regionally-resident storage options, including EU-only data planes. For Dedicated and Private you control the region entirely. We also provide contractual commitments for residency in enterprise contracts.
[07:38] Ethan: Performance question - if we run with masking and redaction, do we see latency impact?
[07:45] Jules: Minimal - redaction is streaming-friendly, we apply token filters during generation to minimize overhead. For heavy custom regex scanning there can be CPU cost; our recommend is to pre-compile rules and use native PII detectors which are optimized. Samir: We can run benchmarks against your typical payloads as part of the POC.
[08:05] Ava: Now switching to the Console audit logs view - this is where you can filter by action type (retention change, legal hold, key rotation) and export CSV.
[08:20] [screen scroll noise]
[08:25] Jules: Here's an example of a retention policy change. You can see who made the change (SSO user), the previous value, and a signature. That ties to RBAC - only users in the admin role can change project-wide retention.
[08:40] Miguel: SSO - do you support SAML and OIDC? We use SAML and SCIM provisioning.
[08:46] Samir: Yes, SAML SSO and SCIM for provisioning. We also support role sync and attribute-based access control.
[08:55] Priya: For private deployment, if we run Redwood on-prem do we still get console features?
[09:02] Jules: Private includes the control plane accesses and console; some hosted-managed services may need connector setup, but you get equivalent UI for data controls and audit access.
[09:12] Lena: Any caveats for PCI scope? We're a payments company and need to limit card data passing through third-party systems.
[09:20] Samir: Important question. If you want to keep card numbers out of any external system, use client-side tokenization or local redaction prior to sending. We also offer an on-prem inference path where data never leaves your network. We have documentation on PCI considerations for LLMs; we'll share that.
[09:37] Miguel: For the POC - we'd like a run with hosted but request-storage off, then a Dedicated run with customer-managed KMS and VPC.
[09:45] Ava: Sounds good. We'll scope the POC: objectives (latency SLO, throughput, and proof of zero-persist of PII), timeline, and success criteria.
[09:57] [discussion of success criteria and timeline]
[12:10] Samir: I'll note two benchmarking targets: 95th percentile latency < 120ms for typical 512-token flows, and support for 30k requests/day with steady-state tail latency under the SLOs.
[12:28] Lena: Budget and pricing concern - if we turn off storage and enable heavy redaction, does cost increase?
[12:35] Jules: Redaction itself has minor CPU overhead; cost impact is generally small. Storage-on vs storage-off affects long-term storage charges. We can show cost delta in the Optimize recommendations during the POC.
[12:50] Priya: Any competitors that do this better? We looked at Anthropic and Bedrock; what are strengths here?
[12:58] Ava: We position Redwood as production-first: granular controls at the API and console layer, unified across hosted/dedicated/private, with explicit auditability and KMS/SSO integrations. Competitors have pieces but not always the integrated retention toggles and observability we demo.
[13:20] Miguel: Ok good. Can you share the SOC2 and ISO reports?
[13:25] Ava: Absolutely. I'll send the security pack and the SOC2 report link after the call.
[13:31] [Questions from Ethan about SDK examples and code snippets]
[13:45] Jules: We'll attach SDK snippets for Java, Python, and a curl quickstart that demonstrates the retention header and redaction flags.
[14:00] Ava: Recap of next steps: send security docs, send retention quickstart, schedule POC kickoff. Anything else?
[14:10] Priya: Please include contact for legal procurement - our procurement lead will want T&Cs and DPA early.
[14:18] Ava: Noted. We'll prep an initial DPA template and pricing estimate.
[14:25] Miguel: One more - can you provide example redaction logs so our compliance folks can see exactly what gets stripped?
[14:33] Samir: We'll produce a sanitized sample set.
[14:36] Lena: Great. Thanks everyone.
[14:40] Ava: Thanks, we'll follow up by end of day tomorrow with the materials.
[14:45] [meeting ends - informal chatter and screenshare stop noise]

Notes: Transcript has occasional misheard product names and caption noise; speakers sometimes overlap. References to 'Redwood Optimize' and 'Redwood Opti-mize' appear in captions.
